# Curlew of Code Updates (`curlew-of-code-updates`)

Shows what a code-set update (CPT, HCPCS, ICD-10) means for you: deleted codes still on open claims, the chargemaster, order sets and fee schedules; new replacement codes with no price; and revised codes to re-describe. You supply the update file from the official release. Patient names on open claims are masked before results reach the model.

**Curlew never changes the chargemaster or fee schedules. Curlew never changes codes on claims; a coder decides.**

Kestrel ver 1 · Money recovery and practice finance · MIT · Node 20 or newer · local files only · patient and staff identifiers masked before results reach the model · built on [`kestrel-core`](../kestrel-core)

```bash
npx -y curlew-of-code-updates demo
npx -y curlew-of-code-updates mcp --root ./practice-files
```

## What the sample data shows

Invented data only. The codes starting with ZZ are made up so that no real CPT, HCPCS or ICD-10 content is shipped; they are not real codes or real changes. Patients are fictional.

- [`code-changes.csv`](fixtures/code-changes.csv): an invented update. Planted against the practice files:
  - Open claim OC-1 (service October 15) uses diagnosis ZZ9.01, deleted from October 1. OC-2 (September 20) is before the change and is fine.
  - ZZ101 and ZZ102 are active on the chargemaster and deleted January 1; ZZ201 is deleted too but already inactive.
  - The "Diabetes follow-up" order set uses ZZ101 and ZZ9.01.
  - ZZ102 is on two payers' fee schedules.
  - New codes ZZ111 (on the chargemaster with no price), ZZ112 and ZZ113 replace codes in use and need a price.
  - ZZ105 is revised.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does | Policy |
|---|---|---|
| `curlew_check` | List deleted codes on open claims, the chargemaster, order sets and fee schedules, new codes with no price and revised codes. | runs |
| `curlew_write_report` | Write curlew-code-updates.csv (one row per item, with blank owner and decision columns) and curlew-code-updates.html into out_dir (default kestrel-out/curlew). | runs |
| `curlew_recall` | Search this agent's own memory of the customer's setup: accepted facts (in use) and facts waiting for a person. | runs |
| `curlew_learn` | Propose one fact about the customer's setup for this agent to remember. | runs |
| `curlew_accept_learning` | A named person accepts or rejects a fact waiting in this agent's memory. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `curlew_retire_memory` | A named person stops an accepted fact from applying. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `chargemaster_update` | Curlew never changes the chargemaster or fee schedules. | refused |
| `claim_recode` | Curlew never changes codes on claims; a coder decides. | refused |

Any tool name not in this table is blocked, including names a model invents. Refused tools are listed so a model can see they exist and are refused.

### `curlew_check` arguments

| Argument | What it is |
|---|---|
| `changes` (required) | Code update file under --root, from the official release you license: code, code set, action (added, deleted, revised), effective date, replacement |
| `chargemaster` (required) | Your chargemaster: code, description, price, active |
| `fee_schedule` | Optional payer fee schedules: payer, code, rate |
| `order_sets` | Optional order sets or templates: order set name, code |
| `open_claims` | Optional open or unbilled claims: claim, patient, date of service, procedure codes, diagnosis codes |
| `status` | Only items with this status |
| `limit` | Most items to return to the model (the report file always has all of them) |

## Columns it reads

Tables can be CSV, TSV, semicolon- or pipe-separated text, Excel `.xlsx`, JSON or JSONL. Columns are matched by the names below (any case and punctuation), and by their usual names in German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Japanese, Chinese and Korean. Dates become `YYYY-MM-DD`. Columns marked *masked* hold patient or staff identifiers.

The PointClickCare, MatrixCare and American HealthTech style names were written from public help pages and general knowledge, **not checked against real exports**. Run `npx curlew-of-code-updates inspect <file>` (column names and shapes only, never values) and name any column it misses in `remedy-sources.json`.

### Code changes (`changes`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `code` (required) | text | Code, CPT, HCPCS, ICD-10, CPT/HCPCS, Procedure Code, Item Code, Charge Code |
| `code_set` | text | Code Set, Type, Code Type, Set, Vocabulary |
| `action` (required) | text | Action, Change, Change Type, Status, Add/Delete/Revise |
| `effective` | date | Effective, Effective Date, Start Date, Release Date |
| `replacement` | text | Replacement, Replaced By, Crosswalk, New Code, Use Instead |
| `description` | text | Description, Descriptor, Short Description |

### Chargemaster (`chargemaster`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `code` (required) | text | Code, CPT, HCPCS, ICD-10, CPT/HCPCS, Procedure Code, Item Code, Charge Code |
| `description` | text | Description, Charge Description, Item Description |
| `price` | amount | Price, Charge, Standard Charge, Gross Charge, Fee |
| `active` | text | Active, Status, Active Flag |

### Fee schedule (`fee_schedule`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `payer` | text | Payer, Payer Name, Primary Payer, Insurance, Insurance Name, Plan, Plan Name, Payor |
| `code` (required) | text | Code, CPT, HCPCS, ICD-10, CPT/HCPCS, Procedure Code, Item Code, Charge Code |
| `rate` | amount | Rate, Allowed, Fee, Contract Rate |

### Order sets (`order_sets`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `order_set` (required) | text | Order Set, Template, Panel, Favorite List, Protocol |
| `code` (required) | text | Code, CPT, HCPCS, ICD-10, CPT/HCPCS, Procedure Code, Item Code, Charge Code |

### Open claims (`open_claims`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `claim_id` | text | Claim, Claim ID, Claim #, Claim Number, Encounter, Encounter ID, Visit ID, Invoice |
| `patient_id` | text (masked) | Patient ID, Patient #, Patient Number, MRN, Medical Record Number, Chart #, Chart Number, Account # |
| `patient_name` | text (masked) | Patient, Patient Name, Name, Client, Client Name, Member, Member Name, Beneficiary |
| `dos` | date | Date of Service, DOS, Service Date, Visit Date, Date, From DOS, Session Date, Appointment Date |
| `codes` | text | Codes, CPT Codes, Procedure Codes, Procedures, CPT |
| `diagnoses` | text | Diagnoses, Diagnosis Codes, ICD-10 Codes, DX, Dx Codes |

## Memory

`curlew_learn` only proposes a fact; nothing changes until a named person accepts it with `curlew_accept_learning`, which is one click even in Auto. Facts live in a hash-chained file under `.remedy/memory/`; if the chain does not verify, no fact is used. Credentials, personal identifiers and text that reads like instructions to an AI are refused.

| Kind | What an accepted fact does |
|---|---|

## Install

Node 20 or newer. No other runtime dependencies besides `kestrel-core` and `remedy-core`.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "curlew-of-code-updates": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "curlew-of-code-updates",
        "mcp",
        "--root",
        "/path/to/practice-files"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Claude Code: `claude mcp add curlew-of-code-updates -- npx -y curlew-of-code-updates mcp --root .`, or use the plugin files in this folder.

## CLI

```bash
curlew-of-code-updates tools                 # every tool, its policy and arguments
curlew-of-code-updates sources               # the columns each input is read from
curlew-of-code-updates inspect <file>        # how a file would be read (names and shapes, never values)
curlew-of-code-updates call curlew_check '{"changes":"<changes>","chargemaster":"<chargemaster>"}'
curlew-of-code-updates eval                  # the private eval cases on the fictional fixtures
curlew-of-code-updates demo
```

## Patient and staff data

Results go to an AI model, so identifiers are masked before they leave the agent: patient and staff names become stable pseudonyms such as `PT-3f9a1c2e`, record and account numbers become `MRN-…` or `ACCT-…`, and e-mails and phone numbers are removed, also inside free text. Report files written to disk keep real names because staff work from them: keep them in a folder only your staff can open. The shared tests check that no fictional identifier from the fixtures reaches any eval result, and the hostile-input check plants spreadsheet formulas, HTML and AI-aimed instructions in the data. This keeps PHI away from the model; it is **not** a HIPAA compliance determination. Your business associate agreements, access controls and policies still apply.

## Limits

- Reads only the files you give it. It does not log in to an EHR, practice-management system, payer portal, clearinghouse, state system, HR or payroll system, or bank.
- Payer, Medicare, Medicaid, state and federal rules are summarised from public material as of 2026, and the numbers are settings you supply; a billing, compliance or legal professional checks them before you rely on them.
- Not legal, billing, coding, tax, clinical or HIPAA advice. It does not diagnose or recommend care. A person decides what to bill, pay, report, file or send.
- Every call is written to a hash-chained audit log under `.remedy/` in the root. No network calls, no telemetry, no credentials. The bundled data is fictional.
